items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was told that Whiteman also owned some stock in this radio station.

ctx.x: of working with us, she became more confident in her work and made less mistakes.

Eventually Evelyn was engaged to do a radio show where Paul Whitman presented an artist every week. I was told that Whiteman also owned some stock in this radio station. Evelyn wanted us to accompany her, but someone at the radio couldn't stand to see three negro musicians accompanying a pretty white woman on that show because it was a broadcast done in a studio where the public were invited to participate.

So the pianist, bassist and a trumpet player from Whiteman's studio orchestra came to the Blue Angel anonymously for a few nights to listen and try to copy the way that we played behind Evelyn. I heard the broadcast because it was before I went to work. Evelyn skipped a measure in one of the songs and the cats accompanying her didn't know how to cover up for her. It must have been embarrassing for all that were concerned in front of a radio public.
